meta.notes: npt: parsed the main table of the English Wikipedia "List of parties to the NPT" (rev 1373395380, 2026-09-05; compiled from the UNODA/depositary records; 190 states) plus North Korea from its separate "Withdrawn state" table (191 in all), and matched the "191 (according to the United Nations)" in the infobox of the main NPT article (rev 1375952857); the list is exactly the 193 UN members minus India, Israel, Pakistan and South Sudan (never signed) plus the observers Holy See and Palestine. North Korea is INCLUDED because the UN/UNODA count of 191 still counts it (it announced withdrawal in 2003; whether that was valid is disputed, the de facto count is 190); drop PRK if you prefer the de facto view. Taiwan (ROC ratified 1970, now abides) is outside the 191 and not in countries.json. Cook Islands and Niue are not parties (they consider themselves bound through New Zealand). No Article X withdrawal notice by any other state (Iran has only threatened, 2025-2026) is recorded on the list as of its latest revision. NPT source licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (English Wikipedia). Dropped (not in countries.json): Holy See. | iaea: parsed the member table of the English Wikipedia "Member states of the IAEA" (rev 1379560340, 2026-10-10) and matched its dated lead "As of September 2026, the IAEA has 182 member states" (same 182 in the infobox of the main IAEA article); iaea.org is 403 to scripts so the organisation's own page was not read. The 182 include the Holy See and the Cook Islands (both full IAEA members; neither is in countries.json); the observer State of Palestine is not counted. Accounting is exact: the 182 members + the 12 UN members with no IAEA relationship + North Korea (withdrew 1994) = the 193 UN members + Holy See + Cook Islands. Recent accessions on the list: Cook Islands (17 October 2024), Maldives (4 December 2025), Somalia (15 November 2024), Timor-Leste (21 September 2026). Caveat: the 182nd member (Timor-Leste, deposit 21 Sep 2026) rests on the US State Department depositary notification 2026-040 (30 Sep 2026) cited by Wikipedia; the IAEA's own member list had not yet been updated for it, and I could not fetch either document (403), so without it the figure would be 181. IAEA source licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (English Wikipedia). Dropped (not in countries.json): Cook Islands, Holy See. | ecosoc: parsed the 2026 row of the UN Dag Hammarskjold Library research guide "ECOSOC Membership by Year" (last updated Sep 25, 2026), whose page states the Council "has 54 members" (UN Charter Art. 61); un.org/ecosoc is 403 to scripts. It matches exactly the Wikipedia "Current members" table (rev 1379588906) once the annotated mid-term swaps are applied: Italy (2025) and Liechtenstein (2024-2025) are gone, the United States (2026-2027) and Germany (2026) are in. Members elected in June 2026 for terms from 1 Jan 2027 are not current and not included. Wikipedia cross-check licence: CC BY-SA 4.0. | Not included: irena (irena.org is 403 to scripts; English Wikipedia has no member list and states only "169 states and the EU (2025)" / "168 states and the EU as of July 2022"; Wikidata has about 7 membership statements, so no list exists that reconciles to a count for the same date; the US announced withdrawal in January 2026, effective date unconfirmed). | Attribution: lists for npt and iaea are taken from English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; contributors listed in each page history at the linked revisions); ecosoc is taken from the UN Dag Hammarskjold Library guide and cross-checked with English Wikipedia.

npt.asOf: status per English Wikipedia revisions of 2026-09-05 (list) and 2026-09-21 (infobox, citing the UNODA treaty database, accessed 2025-11-01); built 2026-10-18

iaea.asOf: September 2026 (English Wikipedia revision 2026-10-10); includes Timor-Leste, whose instrument was deposited 21 Sep 2026
